title: Power Rankings: Mavs start second half on top
heading: 2005-06 Power Rankings: Week 16

rankings.summaryHtml: Since Kobe punked them for 62, Mavs have responded by going 23-4. Since Dampier became a sub, Mavs are 15-1 and have allowed 100 points just once.
rankings.summaryText: Since Kobe punked them for 62, Mavs have responded by going 23-4. Since Dampier became a sub, Mavs are 15-1 and have allowed 100 points just once.

rankings.summaryHtml: Health and holding off Mavs and Spurs for home-court advantage are all that matter now. Unless you think Pistons have a 28-3 run in them.

rankings.summaryHtml: Dismiss them at your own peril. As fragile as Spurs seem with Duncan and Manu at less than 100 percent, they're on pace to break the franchise record for wins (62).

rankings.summaryHtml: No joke: I think Suns can get to the Finals even without Stoudemire, assuming they get all the way to the West finals and let Mavs and Spurs beat each other up first.

rankings.summaryHtml: My favorite Nets fan, Sanford, is livid about Kidd's All-Star snub, with Jersey leading its division, but I bet Kidd benefits from a weekend off as much as anyone.

rankings.summaryHtml: Between now and April 1, Heat have only four games (out of 18) against teams with winning records. Let's see whether they can stay serious when the schedule is soft.

rankings.summaryHtml: Logic tells you Paul's myriad injuries and rising expectations could cause young Hornets to crumble, but I'm gullible enough to believe in their Cinderella mojo.

rankings.summaryHtml: The reward for being the best Clips ever? Mavs or Spurs in the first round unless they either pass Suns with all these moves they're making ... or drop a slot or two.

rankings.summaryHtml: Cavs are just 13-11 without Hughes. But let's set the bar high for the All-Star Game MVP and demand no worse than a 19-11 finish from LBJ's Cavs to get to 50 wins.

rankings.summaryHtml: What a difference a trade makes. Peja already has four 20-point games in his 5-2 start as a Pacer -- after zero 20-point games in the month of January.

rankings.summaryHtml: Grizz return to work with the NBA's stingiest defense (87.7 ppg) and the first All-Star in club history (Pau). That's why they're giddier than your typical No. 7 seed.

rankings.summaryHtml: I don't see any 25-4 runs in their immediate future, but I'd bank on a big finish from a motivated 'Melo ... if rumor-weary Nuggets can regroup after the deadline.

rankings.summaryHtml: Time to solidify their playoff position? Banged-up Bucks reconvened after the All-Star break with a full complement of players for the first time all season.
